item.title: Man in his 60s dies in County Westmeath crash
item.description: A man in his 60s has died after a crash involving two cars in County Westmeath. The crash happened at Cushinstown, Killucan shortly before a quarter past 2 on Friday afternoon. Two cars collided on the Royal Canal Way. Advertisement Following the collision one of the drivers, a man in his 60s, became unwell and was pronounced dead at the scene a short time later. None of the other people in the car needed treatment. The scene has been examined and the local Coroner has been notified. Advertiseme

item.title: Concert in memory of late Des Guckian to take place tonight
item.description: A concert is taking place in memory of Leitrim councillor Des Guckian this evening. He was a member of Annaduff Church Choir before he died in May, while aged in his 70s. The choir is holding a concert in Annaduff church at 7.30 tonight, in aid of North West Hospice. Advertisement It's in memory of Des and another choir member, Michael John Faughnan. These choir members have been remembering Des.

item.title: HSE issues festive season health advice for Shannonside region
item.description: The HSE is advising people in the Shannonside region to keep well and to know where to go if you need urgent care this festive season. Emergency departments are expected to be busy, so consider visiting a local injury unit or pharmacy for minor injuries. Out-of-hours GP services like NowDoc and MidDoc are available, but you must make an appointment. Advertisement You can also access a range of support and advice at your local pharmacy. item.title: Bird flu has limited impact on turkey sales according to local butcher
item.description: A local butcher says bird flu hasn't impacted turkey sales too much this Christmas. There were outbreaks among turkey flocks in the likes of Carlow and Meath last month. That lead to concerns that there would be a shortage of turkeys for sale this month. Advertisement Fianna Fáil Councillor Martin Monaghan runs a butcher shop on Killashee Street in Longford Town. He says he hasn't encountered too many problems in the lead up to Christmas.

item.title: Benches stolen from Doon Shore in Boyle
item.description: Benches have been stolen from the Doon Shore in Boyle, a popular amenity in County Roscommon. The area is widely used by families, clubs, and visitors, particularly during the summer months. In an online post, Lough Key Swim Club said the "benches were bolted to the ground so who ever stole them went there with the intention of stealing them, it wasn’t an opportunist, somebody came prepared." item.title: Leitrim take steps never to concede another game
item.description: Leitrim county board chairman Declan Bohan says steps have been taken to prevent a repeat of Leitrim surrendering a national league game. Indeed, Leitrim conceded their league game with Fermanagh, citing a lack of available players. “It was a very difficult time" explained Bohan. The county chair went on, "It was a low point in terms of you know for everybody". item.title: 'A very, very emotional evening' - huge crowd attends Des Guckian memorial concert
item.description: Around 300 people attended a concert in Annaduff Church, Co Leitrim, tonight in memory of former councillor Des Guckian. He was a member of Annaduff Church Choir before he died in his 70s in May. The choir starred in tonight's concert, which was also in memory of another member, Michael John Faughnan.
